## Status

Plumbing phase complete and validated. The full pipeline going from: raw data acquisition -> fixed-width LMF parsing -> PHQ-9 scoring -> covariate construction -> survey design weighting, reproduces a published NCHS benchmark exactly.

## Validation: reproducing a published estimate

To check whether the full pipeline is working, I reproduced the headline estimate from Brody, Pratt, and Hughes (2018), *Prevalence of Depression Among Adults Aged 20 and Over: United States, 2013-2016* (NCHS Data Brief No. 303: 8.1% weighted prevalance of PHQ-9 >=10 ("depression") among adults aged 20 and over, using pooled NHANES 2013-2016 cycles.

Applying my pipeline to the same population (cycles H and I, ages 20+, MEC exam weight divided by 2 to reflect the two-cycle pool) produced an identical estimate: **8.1%**.

This confirms the weighting, survey design, and PHQ-9 scoring logic are all functioning correctly, end to end, against an independent external benchmark rather than only internal consistency checks. 

## Next steps

Cox proportional hazards model construction, using the full seven-cycle pooled dataset and design object.
